newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks close unmoved in show of strength.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks close unmoved in show of strength.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed barely moved on Tuesday for the third day in a row, showing signs of consolidating after a two-week plunge, brokers said.
The Colombo Stock Exchange all share index closed 0.9 points lower at 605.2 poin5w in lacklustre trading which saw investors sidelined ahead of the upcoming holiday season, they said.
"Investors don't want to get into new positions right now. It's a seasonal thing," said broker Rohan Fernando of CT Smith. "Also they may be waiting for the market to come down further."
"As the 600-point barrier approaches, more and more people will start looking at the market," said Sanjeeva Gunewardena, manager of institutional sales at Commercial Stock Brokers.

Tuesday's turnover was down to 11.2 million rupees from 63.4 million the day before. The only trades that contributed substantially to turnover were 126,000 Saylan Bank at 26 rupees and 230,000 Ceylon Grain Elevators at 10 rupees.
Losses outnumbered gains 20 to 15. Blue chip Hayleys shed five rupees to 180 rupees. Tea Smallholder Factories gained 1.75 to 25 rupees.
